subject: Mediation + Moderation w/ an ordered multicategorical var in lavaan

messages.author: d49dfdba80acf71f
messages.subject: Mediation + Moderation w/ an ordered multicategorical var in lavaan
parts:
Hello Dr. Rosseel,

 

I hope this email finds you well. I have a question on specifying mediation and moderation for ordinal variables in lavaan.

 

I have x1, x2, m, and y where m is an ordered three-level categorical variable. The model is as follows.

 

m ~ a*x1

y ~ c*x1 + x2 + b*m + x2:m

 

Since m is an ordinal variable,  we cannot create this x2:m interaction. Additionally, in y ~ x1 + x2 + b*m + x2:m, I would like to specify a “b” path, but I am unsure whether this is the right way.

 

Thanks,

 

Clare McCann

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Mediation + Moderation w/ an ordered multicategorical var in lavaan
parts:
Hello Clare,

I don't know the 'mediation literature' very well, and perhaps a 'good
practice' for this setting has been described elsewhere.

But I don't see an easy solution. I would try to find a numerical coding
for the ordinal variable (m) that is realistic (perhaps simply 1,2,3;
but maybe 1,2,5 is better; you can also center: -1,0,1) and then treat m
as pseudo-continuous. That would at least allow you to create the
interaction term.

If the interaction is important, then ignoring this interaction term
seems more harmful to me than treating an ordinal variable as continuous.

Yves.

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: Mediation + Moderation w/ an ordered multicategorical var in lavaan
parts:
Hi,

 

I would start by thinking really hard if you need a nonlinear model for m and if you can assume interval scaling of m when used it as a predictor. If yes to both questions, you can use lavaan for the analysis. Regression diagnostics (residual-vs-fited plots, added variable plots) should give you some indication.

 

If either of these assumptions fail, lavaan is not the right tool for the job. Instead, I would recommend the mediation package, which does nonlinear mediation models.

 

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mediation/vignettes/mediation.pdf

 

For an explanation of what these nonlinear mediation models do, see

 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IaPmGw0xr60

 

and

 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ama6EseGYho

 

The first video talks about the general idea of causal mediation and the second about applications to nonlinear models.

 

Mikko
